summary: HE.8 target-level refinement of the accepted HE.7s packet. Reuse its 49 HE.8 target/API nodes (excluding the separate parity target) and its six planets without redefining them. Add eight missing proof interfaces: the clean traced norm module, the adelic/local toric fibre, the arithmetic joining application, the weaker fixed-torsion CM trace theorem, weak-torsion shifted-conductor descent, clean Howard A–D verification, actual perfect character base change, and broadened integral determinant containment. Main-conjecture implications remain conditional; proofs of those conjectures belong to HE.8b. Complete means target coverage, not formalisation or gap-free mathematical closure.

nodes.title: The traced Heegner norm module over K∞
nodes.statement: Assume Howard’s ordinary Heegner setting: E/ℚ of conductor N; K imaginary quadratic of odd discriminant D_K<0, D_K≠−3, all primes of N split; odd p∤ND_K, good ordinary reduction, G_K-image GL₂(ℤ_p), p∤h_K, and total ramification at the p-adic places in K∞/K. Write K_k for its degree-p^k layer, G=Gal(K[1]/K), and Λ=ℤ_p⟦Γ⟧. Define H_k inside E(K_k)⊗ℤ_p as the Λ-submodule generated by Tr_(K[1]/K)P[1] and Tr_(K_k[1]/K_k)P_j[1] for 0≤j≤k, using the accepted conductor-one family P_j[1]. Corestriction restricts to H_(k+1)→H_k; H=lim_k H_k has its actual level projections. It is the traced module over K∞, distinct from H[1] over K∞[1]. The traced chosen Q[1] gives κ̃₁∈H. Howard Theorem 2.3.7 identifies H as a free rank-one Λ-module generated by κ̃₁, with injective inverse-limit Kummer map sending κ̃₁ to the accepted bottom Selmer class. No unit assertion about aug(Φ) is made.
hypotheses: All arithmetic hypotheses and coefficient/local-condition conventions in the statement are required.

sources.match: The proof uses the traced modules, the finite class-group norm, an augmentation image and Nakayama; it does not identify H with H[1].

proofSteps: Restrict the actual corestrictions to the displayed generating sets and form their compact inverse limit using the existing owner’s construction.

Apply the fixed-torsion CM trace theorem through the accepted tower-trace target. Verify the Perrin–Riou rank comparison that Howard cites (Proposition 10, §3) with these modules; the original passage remains an acquisition/interface gap.
In the free presentation use the surjective norm diagram H̃→H[1], H̃^G→H, with vertical maps Norm_G. Since |G| is a p-adic unit, taking G-invariants is exact here.

Identify H̃^G/(γ−1)H̃^G with aug(Φ)H̃^G_0 using the recurrence and the kernel argument of Lemmas 2.3.8–2.3.9. The image of the traced lift generates this module even if aug(Φ) is not a unit. Nakayama gives generation of H, and rank one gives freeness.
acceptance: The finite subgroup and trace are retained in the module and the Kummer comparison.
This clean rank/generator argument is not extended to p|h_K by dividing by |G|. The broad accepted non-torsion assertion has its separate construction.

uses.how: The geometric non-torsion trace identifies the rank of H, rather than H[1].
The traced presentation and its augmentation quotient establish that κ̃₁ is a generator.
The inverse-limit Kummer map identifies the clean branch with the cohomological bottom class.

api.statement: The Norm_G map H[1]→H is the map induced by the levelwise field traces; it carries the chosen Q[1] to κ̃₁ and commutes with Kummer.

tests.name: tracedNormModule_trivial_class_group
tests.statement: If G is trivial, Norm_G=id and the traced level modules coincide with H_k[1]; no extra class-number factor appears.

tests.name: tracedNormModule_trace_scale
tests.statement: For p=5 and a trivial-action free ℤ_5 module with G cyclic of order 2, Norm_G sends x to 2x. Replacing this trace by the identity loses the normalization even though both generate the same line.

tests.name: tracedNormModule_nonunit_augmentation
tests.statement: For the free presentation with inert p=5,a_p=1, aug(Φ)=35. The image lattice is 35ℤ_5 x^G, not ℤ_5 x^G; a generator of this image does not make 35 a unit.

tests.name: tracedNormModule_bad_class_number
tests.statement: For G cyclic of order 5 over ℤ_5, the normalized average Norm_G/5 is not an integral group-ring operator; the clean invariant-exactness argument cannot be invoked.

nodes.title: Adelic norm fibres and expanding P-isogeny annuli
nodes.statement: Fix the actual CV data: F totally real, K/F CM, a prime P of F, a quaternion algebra B split at P and with K embedded, a compact open level H, the relative ring-class tower, a nonempty finite collection 𝒮 of allowed reduction sets S, and a finite set R of shifts distinct modulo Gal_K^(P-rat). For each S, exclude P, require B split and K nonsplit at its primes and |S|+|Ram_f(B)|+[F:ℚ] even. Retain the central norm-component spaces in the accepted joint-CM reduction target. Their fixed norm-component fibres are finite unions of compact quotients Γ_(S,g)\SL₂(F_P), with arithmetic lattices and commensurators identified. For each compact open Galois averaging subgroup G and compact open level H, a fixed P-isogeny class has the parametrization of CV Propositions 2.12 and 2.28: finitely many x_i and one-parameter unipotent groups u_i, and a compact open multiplicative subgroup κ⊂F_P^×, such that its G/level saturation is the union over i and n≥0 of G·x_i·u_i(ϖ^(−n)κ)·H. For fixed i,n this set is the single double orbit G·x_i u_i(ϖ^(−n))·H. The sets ϖ^(−n)κ⊂F_P are expanding annuli, carrying the additive Haar measure used in the subsequent integration. CM conductor tending to infinity escapes compact subsets of that isogeny class. The torus subgroup is not replaced by an arbitrary additive ball.
hypotheses: The hypotheses and conventions in this statement are part of the target.
proofSteps: Import the existing AdelicAlgebraicGroups strong-approximation and anisotropic quotient contracts.
Identify local stabilizers and commensurators through the quaternion order.
Parametrize the toric orbit by the finite unipotent charts, with κ⊂F_P^× and the single-double-orbit identity. Verify conductor escape and the additive Haar normalization on these annuli.
acceptance: κ is multiplicative in F_P^×; its scaled annuli are then integrated with additive Haar measure on F_P. It is not a subgroup of K_P^× or an arbitrary additive ball.
The norm component is fixed before applying Haar distribution.

sources.locator: Proposition2.12 pp.275–276; Lemmas2.19–2.20 pp.280–282; Proposition2.28 pp.287–289.
sources.match: Strong approximation gives the local quotient fibres; the torus calculation expresses conductor growth as translated annuli.

nodes.title: Noncommensurable CM joining and dense unipotent orbit
nodes.statement: In a component fibre of the simultaneous CV reduction space, pairwise distinct shifts modulo Gal^{P-rat}_{K} exclude the proper pairwise commensurable joinings. After the source’s local torus parametrization, for almost every averaging parameter the diagonal unipotent orbit is dense in the product of the cocompact SL₂(F_P)-lattice quotients. The exceptional Galois averaging parameters lie in a countable union of cosets of Gal_K^(P-rat) in Gal_K^ab, negligible for Haar measure as in CV Proposition 2.24. These cosets arise from countably many F_P^×-cosets in K_P^× in the local calculation. Use the exact p-adic orbit-closure/stabilizer classification and partition-diagonal argument, rather than real Ratner or independent density of each coordinate.
hypotheses: The hypotheses and conventions in this statement are part of the target.
proofSteps: Import the requested p-adic orbit-classification statement and twisted-diagonal stabilizer consequence.
Use partition-diagonal subgroups and closed-orbit commensurability to identify every proper joining.
Use the P-rational distinctness of shifts and Proposition 2.24’s countable Haar-null Gal_K^(P-rat)-cosets to exclude these joinings almost everywhere.
acceptance: Marginal density alone is insufficient for a product joining.
The finite-extension F_P version is an explicit supplier obligation, not inferred from a Q_p-only citation.

sources.locator: Propositions 2.22 and 2.24, printed pp.282–286; Lemmas 2.30–2.32 and Corollary 2.34/Proposition 2.35, printed pp.289–292, §2.5/§2.7.
sources.match: Orbit classification plus the quaternionic commensurator description rules out proper joinings; the rational and finite-extension input boundary is recorded separately.

nodes.title: Cornut–Vatsal nonzero fixed-torsion CM trace
nodes.statement: In the indefinite quaternionic CV setting assume H2: at each Q≠P ramified in K/F, B_Q is split and R_Q maximal. Let π:J↠A be a nonzero surjective rational Pic(O_F)-equivariant quotient with A=A{ω}, and choose χ on G0 inducing ω^ε on G2. For all but finitely many x∈CM(P∞), Σ_{σ∈G0}χ(σ)σ·α(x)/|G0| is nonzero in A⊗_{Z{ω}}C. H1 and P-newness are not needed for this fixed-torsion projection theorem. For Howard’s F=Q modular quotient, use trivial torsion type to obtain a non-torsion trace at some sufficiently high conductor.
hypotheses: The hypotheses and conventions in this statement are part of the target.
proofSteps: Use H2 degeneracy maps to remove the G1/G2 contribution without losing surjectivity; import their quaternionic Hecke realization.
For the remaining G0/G1 shifts use eventual independent reduction on compatible components.
Choose an inert auxiliary reduction prime with supersingular fibres larger than the fixed map-degree times the finite torsion bound, via the requested quantitative class-set growth.
Conclude the assumed torsion projection cannot vanish for all sufficiently high CM points.
acceptance: A rational-character denominator is not asserted to be a p-adic unit.
This theorem does not depend on an anticyclotomic main conjecture.

sources.locator: Theorem4.10 p.41; Lemmas4.14–4.16 pp.44–48; Proposition4.17 and end of proof pp.49–50.
sources.match: The fixed-torsion trace is the statement used by Howard; the proof uses simultaneous reduction and a finite-fibre contradiction.

nodes.title: Weak-torsion descent and shifted-conductor verification
nodes.statement: In the ordinary Heegner setting of CGLS §4.1 with E(K)[p]=0, and without p∤h_K or full G_K-image, put d(k)=min{d≥0:K_k⊂K[p^d]} and P_k[n]=Tr_(K[np^d(k)]/K_k[n])P[np^d(k)]. For each admissible squarefree n and each coefficient quotient by the actual I_n, establish the auxiliary disjointness/invariant-vanishing that makes restriction H¹(K,T/I_nT)→H¹(K[n],T/I_nT)^{Gal(K[n]/K)} an isomorphism. Verify the pro-p base-tower vanishing E(K∞)[p]=0, the actual transition squares for these shifted P_k[n], and the common-presentation finite solvability used by universal-norm-heegner-family with finite G0 retained. These checks provide that accepted construction and derivative restriction API in the weak-torsion branch; no rank or main-conjecture endpoint is replanned. Do not use the integral average 1/|G0| when p divides |G0|.
hypotheses: All arithmetic hypotheses and coefficient/local-condition conventions in the statement are required.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.1.1, §4.1, published pp.566–568; d(k), equations (4.1)–(4.3) and restriction comparison on p.567.
sources.match: The weak-torsion adaptation needs these arithmetic comparisons; a formal substitution of d(k) in the clean proof does not discharge them.

proofSteps: Use the p-group fixed-vector argument for E(K∞)[p]=0. Obtain the exact auxiliary disjointness and invariant-vanishing from the HE.4 extension request, and apply inflation–restriction with both end terms checked.
Track finite G0 and the actual inclusions K_k⊂K[p^d(k)] in the point traces. Prove the common free-presentation finite constraints with those maps, not with the clean tower’s k+1 indexing.

Check the ordinary local descent using the semilocal norm comparison at p; its finite residue torsion term is retained. Supply these verification data to the already accepted family and restriction APIs.
acceptance: A pro-p fixed-vector argument alone does not prove auxiliary ring-class disjointness.
The weak-torsion localized divisibility theorem remains separate from integral Howard Theorem B.

nodes.title: Arithmetic verification of Howard’s abstract bound
nodes.statement: Assume the full clean arithmetic hypotheses of howard-traced-universal-norm-module. For T=T_pE⊗Λ with the fixed inverse tautological Γ-action and Howard’s propagated ordinary self-dual local conditions, verify hypotheses A–D of EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.8/self-dual-lambda-adic-kolyvagin-bound: S is Λ-torsion-free; normalized height-one specialization/control has finite kernel and cokernel and bounded lattice index outside a finite exceptional set; specialized coefficients and local conditions satisfy Howard’s actual H0–H5; and char_Λ(X_tors) is invariant under ι(γ)=γ^−1 through the arithmetic functional equation. Specify the same local conditions in that functional equation and in the height-one maps. Local p-torsion/component effects are finite control errors, not assumed zero. This is the arithmetic verification input to the accepted Theorem B endpoint, without restating that endpoint or importing it as a proof prerequisite.
hypotheses: The hypotheses and conventions in this statement are part of the target.
proofSteps: Import HE.5’s actual H0–H5 checks, retaining its χ comparison gap.
Apply local control with finite reduction errors and the stated normalized height-one maps.
Verify the exact complementary local conditions required by the arithmetic functional equation and identify its characteristic-ideal consequence.
acceptance: Howard’s height-one comparison excludes pΛ where stated.
Rubin’s admissible Z_p-extension hypothesis is not imposed: auxiliary inert primes split completely here.

At an inert auxiliary prime the infinite-decomposition hypothesis of SI.L3/universal-norms-unramified is unavailable: use the accepted Heegner local verification for that case, not this generic shortcut.
The Shapiro convention is reconciled with Howard’s direct action through the ι-semilinear comparison; α and α^−1 are not silently exchanged.

sources.locator: Proposition2.1.3 pp.23–24; Lemma2.2.7/Proposition2.2.8/Lemma2.2.9 pp.25–26; proof of Theorem2.3.1 pp.27–28.
sources.match: These are the arithmetic verifications for the generic A–D theorem; invariance needs the functional equation, not a formal module decomposition.

nodes.title: Perfect character base change for the arithmetic complex
nodes.statement: For CS’s actual all-p strict ordinary Selmer complex C=RΓ_f(K,T_pE⊗Λ), with its global-to-local cone, unramified inertia terms away from p and ordinary quotient terms at every v|p, assume (Heeg),(disc), odd p∤ND_K, good ordinary reduction and E(K)[p]=0. Prove perfectness over Λ and, for every continuous α:Γ→ℤ_p^× sufficiently close to 1, the arithmetic derived comparison C⊗^L_(Λ,α)ℤ_p≃RΓ_f(K,T_pE(α)), using the same ordinary/inertia local maps and preserving their H⁰ and Tor terms. The induced inverse-determinant isomorphism transports the integral lattice and, where the rational rank-one tensor identification is defined, the Heegner tensor. This refines the accepted determinant-specialization-lattice proof input, rather than asserting that finite-layer control already covers character evaluation. The Nekovář 8.10.1 theorem used by CS is requested from SI.L3; its proof was not independently read in this run.
hypotheses: The hypotheses and conventions in this statement are part of the target.
proofSteps: Import the exact perfect character-specialization theorem through the SI.L3 request.
Verify every local ordinary/inertia map and its specialization compatibility for the stated arithmetic representation.

Apply the generic determinant functor only after the arithmetic derived equivalence has been established. Then compare its rational identification with the accepted Heegner determinant tensor, keeping ι/α^−1 conventions.
acceptance: Finite generation is insufficient for perfectness.
Tor and local-change terms are preserved until the asserted derived comparison establishes the correct lattice.
No localization cokernel or bad-place determinant term is suppressed in the local comparison. The asymmetric split Greenberg complex of BCGS is a different complex.

sources.locator: Equation(3.17), Corollary3.3.4 proof p.16, referring to Nekovář8.10.1.
sources.match: Character specialization is a derived determinant comparison for a perfect complex, not a bare H¹ tensor identity.

nodes.title: Integral containment under the CS surjective hypotheses
nodes.statement: Under (Heeg),(disc), p>3 ordinary unramified, residual G_Q-image GL₂(F_p) and p∤c_φ, verify the arithmetic Λ-bound needed to place z_{K∞} inside det^{-1}C, without assuming p∤h_K. This entails the broader d(k) construction, the full integral self-dual A–D control and the exact ordinary lattice comparison; a divisibility proved only in Λ[1/p,1/(γ−1)] is insufficient. The containment proves one side of the basis proposition and is an input to the converse refined-index implication. It is not an assertion that clean Howard Theorem B already has these weaker tower hypotheses.
hypotheses: The hypotheses and conventions in this statement are part of the target.
proofSteps: Check residual-to-p-adic image and local control hypotheses for this arithmetic representation.

Verify the broadened arithmetic A–D hypotheses at every height-one prime, including pΛ and the augmentation prime, through the exact ES.8/SI.L3 contracts. The clean howard-specialization-hypotheses node is a comparison case, not a theorem applied outside its hypotheses.
Translate the product of Heegner index ideals into an integral determinant containment.
acceptance: Localized CGLS divisibility cannot substitute for integral containment.
This target is explicitly open at the expanded arithmetic-interface verification.
The lower integral divisibility is independent of the main-conjecture equality. Introducing that equality as a prerequisite would make the converse equivalence circular.
Residual G_Q surjectivity, restriction to G_K and the full p-adic image implication are checked with p>3 and p∤D_K; they are not equated by notation.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem C, §3.4 p.17, invoking Howard Theorem B; compare Howard Theorem B p.3 and CGLS Theorem4.1.2 p.568.
sources.match: The converse needs integral containment; the source’s invocation must be reconciled with the clean class-number condition through an explicit broadened arithmetic verification.

requests.need: Homogeneous-dynamics Part II contract: for L a finite extension of Q_p, G=SL₂(L), X=∏_{i=1}^r Γ_i\G with cocompact arithmetic lattices, V={v(t)} a one-parameter L-unipotent subgroup of G^r, each orbit closure is xH for a closed H⊃V and has its normalized H-invariant probability θ_x. For continuous f and every compact κ⊂L of positive additive Haar measure, |s|→∞ gives λ(sκ)^{-1}∫_{sκ}f(xv(t))dλ(t)→∫f dθ_x. For V=ΔU the measure stabilizer contains cΔG c^{-1} with c∈U^r. Export the pairwise-commensurability/partition-diagonal joining consequence. This is CV-CM Theorem2.29/Lemma2.30, p.289; the Q_p case cites Ratner Duke Math.J.77(1995), Corollary4 of Theorem6; the S-arithmetic/finite-extension supplier must verify the precise Ratner and Margulis–Tomanov Invent.Math.116(1994) hypotheses. Existing GN.4 is real-only and does not yet supply it.
Reuse the existing anisotropic compact quotient theorem for B_S and identify the finite union of cocompact local SL₂(F_P)-lattice quotients in CV-CM Lemmas2.19–2.20, pp.280–282.

Reuse current upstream simply connected strong approximation with noncompact factor outside S to obtain the exact quaternionic fibre and commensurator description of CV-CM Lemmas2.19–2.20. Keep the central reduced-norm component; do not re-plan strong approximation.

Reuse the existing supersingular-reduction owner for the exact CV-CM §3 local quaternionic fibre model: Proposition 3.9 and Corollary 3.10, printed pp.297–298. Retain the central norm component and flip exactly the reduction prime and archimedean ramification. This is a refinement of HE.7s’s request, not a new canonical-model theory.

Quantitative supersingular norm-fibre growth used in CV Theorem 4.10 proof, preprint pp.49–50: for each fixed finite degree d and tower torsion bound t choose suitable inert good reduction primes with every relevant fibre cardinality >td. Supply the component-aware class-set/mass/point-count comparison through the existing definite quaternionic owner.

H2 ramified-prime degeneracy maps preserving Pic(O_F)-equivariance and the nonzero/surjective quotient in CV Lemmas 4.14–4.16, preprint pp.44–48. Only the fixed-torsion Theorem 4.10 branch is a new consumer here; P-new/type-I/II primitive-character interfaces remain in HE.7s.

Refine the existing Howard norm-module request to the traced module H over K∞: verify the universal-norm rank comparison quoted as Perrin–Riou (1987), Proposition 10 of §3, and compact inverse-limit/presentation exactness used in Howard Theorem 2.3.7 and Lemmas 2.3.8–2.3.9, PDF pp.34–35. Supply the stated finite class-group norm diagram and augmentation kernel comparison, without asserting aug(Φ) is a unit. The original Perrin–Riou proof remains unread here.

Refine the accepted character/control request: establish Nekovář 8.10.1 coefficient-character derived specialization for the actual ordinary/inertia maps of CS equation (3.17), PDF p.16, with perfectness and H⁰/Tor retained; verify Howard’s exact arithmetic functional equation and normalized height-one errors under the clean hypotheses. For CS integral containment supply the full integral self-dual local-condition comparison at pΛ and augmentation as well, not just rational duality. Finite-layer derived control is already planned and is reused. For broader-tower-descent-verification also supply the actual semilocal ordinary norm comparison at p in the shifted d(k) tower, preserving its finite residue torsion term.

Refine the full-image HE.4 torsion-invariants result to the actual weak-torsion CGLS §4.1 tower: prove auxiliary K[n]/K versus ℚ(E[p]) disjointness, invariant vanishing and inflation–restriction for the completed coefficient quotients in equation (4.3), published p.567. Record the base pro-p torsion comparison and the actual d(k) maps.

The self-dual-lambda-adic-kolyvagin-bound node is reused. Supply its exact integral application contract for CS §3.4 under residual surjectivity and d(k), without a p∤h_K hypothesis: verify A–D at all height-one primes using the actual propagated ordinary Heegner strong system. This is the explicit gap between clean Howard Theorem B (PDF p.3) and CGLS’s localized Theorem 4.1.2 (published p.568); do not replace integral containment by that localization.
